In the Deferred Acceptance (DA) algorithm, my goal is to maximize my chances of being matched with the most preferred school possible. My preference order is x > z > y > w, and I have a high priority at both w and y (rank 1), and a lower priority at x and z (rank 2). 

Given that most applicants prefer y > x > w > z, school y is likely to be very competitive. However, I have the highest priority at y, which gives me a significant advantage there. Similarly, I have the highest priority at w, which could be a safe fallback option if my higher preferences don't work out.

1. I will first propose to x, my top choice. Despite having a lower priority there, if other applicants prioritize y first, I might have a chance if x has fewer applicants or if some applicants get accepted elsewhere.
2. If rejected from x, I will propose to z next. Although I have the same priority at z as x, it is less preferred by others, increasing my chances of acceptance.
3. If rejected from z, I will propose to y. I have the highest priority at y, so I am very likely to be accepted unless all spots are filled by other high-priority applicants.
4. Finally, if rejected from y, I will propose to w. I have the highest priority at w, so I am almost guaranteed a spot there.

My strategy is to aim for my most preferred schools initially, and leverage my high priority at y and w as a safety net.
